_meta.purpose: Inputs for FarmSight Layer 2 (sell/hold) and Layer 3 (arbitrage). Every value has a source and confidence. Replace ASSUMPTION items with real quotes when available.

confidence_scale.high: official document or official announcement read directly
confidence_scale.medium: reported by a reputable news outlet, not checked against the primary source
confidence_scale.derived: computed from sourced values with the stated formula
confidence_scale.assumption: no source found; placeholder that must be confirmed

_meta.units: Rs per 40kg (maund) unless stated. NOTE: AMIS price file is Rs per 100kg. Multiply AMIS by 0.4 to compare.

sbp_policy_rate_pct.note: sbp.org.pk returned 403 when fetched, so not verified on the SBP site. Check after the 26 Oct meeting.

holding_interest_rate_pct_per_year.formula: policy rate 11.5 + 5.0 spread. The Agriculture Policy Institute prices farm credit as KIBOR + 5% in its cost tables; KIBOR approximated by the policy rate because no KIBOR figure was found.

diesel_rs_per_litre.note: Prices change almost daily under the current pricing system.

usd_pkr_interbank.note: Source text was garbled (shows 77.05 beside previous close 277.06). Value read as 277.05.

FY2024_avg.note: From memory of the PBS figure, not confirmed in this research. Verify against PBS.

FY2025_avg.note: Sources conflict between calendar and fiscal year. Verify against PBS.

sep_2026_yoy.note: Figure appeared in a search summary of the SBP-related coverage

2021-22.note: AMIS official support-price table (Rs per 40 kg).

2022-23.note: AMIS official support-price table (Rs per 40 kg). Earlier left unset because news sources conflicted (2,200 vs 3,900); AMIS mandi prices in Apr-Jun 2023 averaged Rs 3,954-4,085, consistent with 3,900.

2023-24.note: Announced at Rs 3,900 by the federal and Punjab governments; Punjab did not buy wheat from farmers. AMIS wheat fell from Rs 3,531 (Apr 2024) to Rs 2,755 (Jun 2024). Corrected 9 Oct 2026: an earlier version filed this under 2024-25, because the USDA source uses marketing year 2024/25 for the spring 2024 harvest.

2024-25.note: AMIS official table shows no value ('-'). No support price announced and no Punjab procurement (IMF-linked deregulation). Market fell to Rs 2,200-2,390 in Apr 2025; AMIS shows Rs 2,300-2,389 for Apr-Jun 2025, which also confirms the per-100kg to per-40kg conversion.

2025-26.note: Described by an official as indicative, not a fixed support price (docs/FACTS.md). Punjab bought at Rs 3,500 in Apr-May 2026; AMIS Apr-Jun 2026 averaged Rs 3,337-3,445.

support_2026_27.status: not announced as of 2026-10-09; Punjab recommends 4200, Sindh 5000, Kissan Ittehad asks 4702-5000

open_market_punjab_2026_10_08.note: Higher than the AMIS prices for the same week (about 3,500-3,820). See data_quality_warnings.

cotton.note: No confirmed phutti support price. A Rs 8,500 per maund stabilisation figure was proposed by the Food Security ministry but its status could not be confirmed. Do not use as a floor.

rice_irri.note: No government support price for paddy.

phutti_market_2026_09_30.note: Cotton Ginners Association data via Business Recorder weekly review.

cost_of_production_punjab._note: Latest OFFICIAL Agriculture Policy Institute (API) tables are 2022-23 (rice, cotton) and 2023-24 (wheat). No official 2025-26 table exists. The 2026 estimate applies cumulative CPI escalation and is a LOWER bound, because fertilizer rose faster than CPI (urea 2,150 to 4,455; DAP 9,000 to 14,259).

estimate_2026_per_acre.formula: official 2023-24 net cost 100,859.18 * 1.045 (FY25 CPI) * 1.071 (FY26 CPI); same method as the per-40kg cross-check

estimate_2026.note: Pakistan Kissan Ittehad (farmer lobby) estimate, 25 Aug 2026. Not itemised.
estimate_2026.cross_check: CPI-escalating the official 2023-24 figure (3,303.52 * 1.045 * 1.071) gives 3,697, within 2% of the lobby figure. Use 3,700 to 3,761.

paddy_to_milled_rice_yield.note: Typical IRRI milling outturn. No source checked. Needed because AMIS rice looks like milled rice while the API cost is per 40kg of paddy.

rice_irri_paddy.caution: Cost is per 40kg of PADDY. Confirm whether the AMIS 'Rice (IRRI)' price is paddy or milled rice before computing margin. AMIS Oct 2026 is about Rs 4,600 per 40kg, which sits between paddy listings (2,200-2,800) and milled listings (5,400-6,000).

official_2022_23.note: Official table is for Basmati in general; used for Super Basmati.

milled_equivalent_rs_per_40kg.formula: 2685 / 0.65 milling yield (assumption; ignores milling cost and by-product value)

storage_rs_per_40kg_per_month.note: No current Pakistani tariff found. A Punjab Agriculture Dept feasibility study assumed Rs 15, 30 and 50 per maund per month but the grain mapping and date are unclear. 15 is the lowest of those. Get a real quote from PASSCO or a local godown.

government_financing_support.note: Punjab said it covers about 70% of financing cost on a KIBOR-linked structure for wheat procurement. This applies to the government procurement scheme, not to a private farmer holding grain.

distance_km.formula: haversine between city coordinates in config.py, times 1.3 road factor

rate_rs_per_40kg_per_km.derivation: 10-tonne truck = 250 maunds. Fuel at about 3 km/L loaded and diesel Rs 395 = Rs 131/km. Fuel taken as about 40% of operating cost, so about Rs 330/km, giving about Rs 1.3 per maund per km. All three assumptions need checking with a real freight quote.
rate_rs_per_40kg_per_km.example: BahawalPur to Vehari 127 km is about Rs 165 per 40kg

data_quality_warnings: AMIS wheat looks sticky/lagging. For 8 Oct 2026 AMIS shows about Rs 3,820 per 40kg (BahawalPur) and Rs 3,475 (RahimYarKhan), while ARY reports the Punjab open market at Rs 5,300. AMIS tracked the Rs 3,500 procurement price well in April 2026. Treat late-2026 wheat points with caution and consider testing the model with and without the last 2 months.
AMIS rice IRRI and Super Basmati unit (paddy vs milled) unconfirmed; price levels look milled. Resolve before any margin calculation.

RahimYarKhan IRRI is nearly empty (dropped). Super Basmati has no prices for 2021-2022 at Vehari and RahimYarKhan, and its latest prices are Nov 2025 (Vehari), Dec 2025 (RahimYarKhan), Apr 2026 (BahawalPur).
All news-based values are medium confidence. Primary SBP site could not be fetched (403).
Cost of production for rice and cotton is a CPI-escalated lower bound, not an official 2025-26 figure.

Wheat support-price years corrected 9 Oct 2026: the Rs 3,900 announced-but-not-procured price belongs to the 2023-24 crop (spring 2024 harvest); the 2024-25 crop (spring 2025 harvest) had no support price.
